USDA Food and Nutrition Service Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program  State Options Report  15th Edition 10 
Certification Periods for Households 
With Simplified Reporting Requirements 
 
State agencies have flexibility in how long they certify SNAP 
households assigned to simplified reporting, which is the most 
common reporting system used. State agencies may certify 
households in which all adult members are 60 or older or have 
disabilities for a maximum of 24 months, and all other 
households for a maximum of 12 months. State agencies must 
certify households for at least 4 months. Some State agencies 
certify all households for the same length of time, while others 
certify households for varying lengths of time. Households 
certified for longer than 6 months must submit a periodic report 
4 to 6 months after certification. Households in which all adult 
members are 60 or older or have a disability, have no earned 
income, and are certified for more than 12 months must file a 
periodic report once a year (State agencies cannot require a 
periodic report from these household more frequently). This 
information does not apply to households assigned to other 
reporting systems, households participating in demonstration 
projects that may extend certification periods, or households 
participating in alternative transitional benefits.
